title: Vegas Part 04: The Poon Poon Report
summary: Episode 116 closes the four-part Las Vegas sequence with a recap of the intoxicated escort guest, deliberate bedside audio capture of a sexual encounter, a detailed commercial-sex review, the guest's confusion over live versus recorded publication, Critter's attempted resignation over the show's turn toward pornography, and a Le Rêve wager that pressures Bill into a photographed body act until he says no. The audit preserves the explicit and offensive dialogue, corrects locally resolvable entities, separates subjective review from fact, and records publication, intoxication, withdrawal, bodily-autonomy and public-discovery boundaries.
source_notes: The raw file has 2,021 segments and approximately 12,169 words; the clean file has 1,998 segments and the same approximate word count across 4,341.54 transcript seconds (4,346.645-second audio). All twenty-three cleaner removals are empty zero-duration artifacts.

Accept DVDASA, Wicked, Critter and David Choe. Reject global `the Bellagio` → `Bellagio`. Context also supports TER, TruthSayers, Preferred 411, Cityvibe, Balboa Island, PMs, neti pot, Le Rêve and Franco Dragone, while remaining corrupt venue/site/private names stay uncertain pending audio verification.

The intimate audio cannot be described as unambiguously consented. A microphone is deliberately placed at the bedside after a speaker says the participants probably do not want audio; others infer consent from prior on-camera conduct. The guest later shows confusion about live versus recorded/edited publication.

During the recorded encounter, the guest says she does not like doggy style, repeats no, and the partner offers to switch. The post-sex report confirms this refusal. This is useful positive evidence amid the larger recording-consent failure.

The guest moves away from the microphone to exchange contact information. Her work alias, review-board identifier, current account status, rates, clients, schedule, lodging and contact routes remain outside public discovery.
The guest is repeatedly described as too intoxicated; the cast imposes a liquor timeout and later offers more alcohol. Self-requested alcohol does not erase capacity concerns.

The Poon Report is a subjective and economically consequential review. The cast calls the encounter a freebie tied to a favorable review and offers to post to the board; the reader must not present the rating as objective product quality.

Critter reads a resignation letter saying the show is turning him into a `porno person`. Others refuse to accept it. Withdrawal from participation does not require group approval, even though he later proposes an off-camera audio role.
The Le Rêve wager is factually resolved: the Wynn production was created by former Cirque du Soleil director Franco Dragone and resembled Cirque, but was not a Cirque du Soleil production.

Neither losing a bet nor another person's willingness grants access to Bill's body. Bill questions whether he gets a say, faces escalating act/photo pressure, forbids tagging, explains privacy harm, and ultimately says no. The cast stops the act and confirms the bet ends because he does not want it.
De-identifying a photograph by omitting a face does not establish permission to capture or publish it. `Do not tag me` is also a direct discoverability boundary.
David's proposal to gamble as an alternative punishment is rejected by others; exploiting a known gambling problem is not an acceptable wager.
Every slur, degrading judgment, stereotype, manipulation admission and contradiction remains literal. Editorial corrections and warnings do not rewrite those ideas.
Named dialogue remains withheld because the diarization file contains zero turns. Window embeddings exist but have not passed independently held-out multispeaker validation.
